hypothesis: Original-pivot exits improve early structural loss control but leave a static floor after an advance. A support line equal to max(original entry pivot, current completed-day MA20) preserves the original floor while tracking later trend support.
unique_change: Exit after the first post-entry close below max(original entry-signal pivot, current causal MA20), using the original next-open fill constraints. The floor never falls below the entry pivot; it may fall with MA20 above that floor. This is not a high-watermark trailing stop.
horizon: Same archived 40-valid-bar endpoint for both arms and all original 4396 entries.
execution: Same independent matcher and entry prices, commission 0.0003, slippage 10 bps, a_share_historical stamp tax, no extra stops or holding-day changes.
terminal_accounting: Real exits retain net proceeds in zero-interest cash until the fixed endpoint. Censored positions mark at endpoint close after entry cost without hypothetical sell cost. Report censor counts separately.
benchmark: Identical archived fixed-horizon equal-weight market return; excess = endpoint wealth / market gross return - 1.

statistics.method: Circular moving blocks of complete signal-date trading calendar; resample same-day sums and counts jointly, event-weighted mean paired excess. Centered two-sided bootstrap p. Exploratory follow-up, not independent confirmation.

required_outputs: entry and baseline-arm parity with v1
success_action: Research support only; separately validate candidate selection, portfolio overlap and unseen data. Do not promote production defaults.
failure_action: Stop this combined support representation and MA-length, pivot-buffer or confirmation-day neighbors; return to entry/selection mechanisms.
previous_evidence: entry-pivot-exit-replacement-v1 improved paired excess but failed nonnegative variant excess and original-positive retention. The current hypothesis changes the moving exit structure, not its numerical thresholds.
